recommendation.headline: Amazfit Balance for tested heart-rate accuracy; Fitbit Air or Garmin vivosmart 5 as cheaper sleep-focused picks
recommendation.summary: Balance has the only explicit tested heart-rate accuracy claim at $199, but sleep accuracy evidence is thin for every option.

reasons.text: HR sensor top-class and accurate in tests

tradeoffs.text: Sleep accuracy not verified; reviewer cites sleep features not accuracy; $199 leaves no margin

alternatives.when: Sleep focus, $99, no screen, no GPS
Want free data and Garmin consistency; check current price

caveats: No independent lab validation in sources
nextSteps: Look for validation studies vs polysomnography

contradictions.topic: Whether Fitbit detailed sleep data is free
contradictions.assessment: PopSci (2023, Inspire 3) says detailed sleep data needs Premium; Tom's Guide (2026, Air) says detailed sleep reports are free. Different devices/dates; Tom's Guide is newer and more reliable (77 vs 59 after verification).

uncertainties.text: Balance HR accuracy comes only from Live Science, a 2022-dated page
No source measures sleep accuracy against a reference
